title: How the Balloon Was Launched, part 1
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: For three days Dorothy heard nothing from Oz. These were sad days for the little girl, although her friends were all quite happy and contented. The Scarecrow told them there were wonderful thoughts in his head; but he would not say what they were because he knew no one could understand them but himself. When the Tin Woodman walked about he felt his heart rattling around in his breast; and he told Dorothy he had discovered it to be a kinder and more tender heart than the one he had owned when he was made of flesh. The Lion declared he was afraid of nothing on earth, and would gladly face an army or a dozen of the fierce Kalidahs.
Thus each of the little party was satisfied except Dorothy, who longed more than ever to get back to Kansas.
On the fourth day, to her great joy, Oz sent for her, and when she entered the Throne Room he greeted her pleasantly:
“Sit down, my dear; I think I have found the way to get you out of this country.”
“And back to Kansas?” she asked eagerly.
“Well, I’m not sure about Kansas,” said Oz, “for I haven’t the faintest notion which way it lies. But the first thing to do is to cross the desert, and then it should be easy to find your way home.”
“How can I cross the desert?” she inquired.

“Well, I’ll tell you what I think,” said the little man. “You see, when I came to this country it was in a balloon. You also came through the air, being carried by a cyclone. So I believe the best way to get across the desert will be through the air. Now, it is quite beyond my powers to make a cyclone; but I’ve been thinking the matter over, and I believe I can make a balloon.”

“A balloon,” said Oz, “is made of silk, which is coated with glue to keep the gas in it. I have plenty of silk in the Palace, so it will be no trouble to make the balloon. But in all this country there is no gas to fill the balloon with, to make it float.”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how long did Dorothy hear nothing from Oz?
options: Three days
A single night
A week
Nearly a month

questions.prompt: Per the passage, why would the Scarecrow not repeat his thoughts?
options: He believed nobody else could understand them
He had forgotten them almost at once
Oz had forbidden him to speak of them
They were too sad to be worth saying

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Woodman say about his new heart?
options: It was kinder and more tender than his old one
It rattled so much he could not sleep
It was smaller than the one he had lost
It made him sorry for every creature

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Lion say he would gladly face?
options: An army or a dozen fierce Kalidahs
The Wicked Witch of the West again
The Winged Monkeys in a body
A field of deadly poppies

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is a balloon made of?
options: Silk coated with glue to hold the gas in
Green paper stretched over wooden slats
Cotton soaked in oil and set alight
Thin tin beaten out and soldered

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is Oz uncertain about Kansas itself?
options: He has not the faintest notion which way it lies
He believes Kansas may not exist at all
He has promised the Witch not to go there
The balloon cannot travel that far

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Oz decide on travel through the air?
options: Both he and Dorothy came to Oz that way
The desert cannot be walked across in any season
The Winged Monkeys refused to carry her
It is the only thing his magic can manage

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is the obstacle to the balloon plan?
options: There is no gas in the country to fill it
There is no silk to be had in the Palace
Nobody knows how to sew the strips together
The desert is too wide for any balloon

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does longed mean?
options: Wished for it very deeply
Waited without much interest
Asked for it again and again
Grew tired of thinking about it

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: Three friends are content while the fourth is offered a plan at last
Three friends discover their gifts were worthless after all
The Wizard refuses to help Dorothy cross the desert
Dorothy decides to stay in the Emerald City for good

questions.prompt: According to the passage, on which day did Oz send for Dorothy?
options: The fourth
The second
The seventh
The very next

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Woodman feel as he walked about?
options: His heart rattling in his breast
The patch pulling at his tin
His joints beginning to rust
Nothing whatever

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did Oz greet Dorothy?
options: Pleasantly, and asked her to sit down
Coldly, without looking up
By pretending to be the great Head
With an apology for the delay

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Oz say must be done first?
options: Cross the desert
Find which way Kansas lies
Make a cyclone like the first
Ask the Winged Monkeys for help

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Oz admit is beyond his powers?
options: Making a cyclone
Making a balloon of silk
Sewing the strips together
Finding gas in the country

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does contented describe about the three friends?
options: Satisfied with what they had been given
Quiet because they had nothing to say
Impatient to leave the city
Sorry for the way Oz had tricked them

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: Contentment for three, and the first real hope for the fourth
A plan to cross the desert that everyone agrees is hopeless
A quarrel about whether the gifts were real
Dorothy's decision to walk across the desert alone
